title: Wiping over socks and bandages (mash)
intro: Allah made wudu easier: we can wipe over leather socks and bandages.

learn.html: Mash means wiping a part of the body, or something on it, with a wet hand. For example, in wudu we wipe part of the head; we can also wipe over khuffs (leather socks) and over a bandage.
Khuffs are light leather socks or slippers. Wiping over them is an easing (rukhsah) in wudu – because of illness, cold weather, travel and so on.

items: After making wudu, the person puts on the khuffs.
When making wudu again, they don’t wash the feet – they wipe over the khuffs with a wet hand.
With the fingers of the right hand we wipe the right khuff from the toes toward the ankle, then with the left hand the left khuff the same way.

learn.text: Wiping over khuffs is not valid if they

items: are too low and don’t cover the ankles
were put on before making wudu

learn.html: Wiping is broken by taking the khuffs off, by the time running out, and by everything that breaks wudu.

learn.title: Bandages
learn.html: Someone with an injury on a part washed in wudu, under a bandage, plaster cast or splint that must not be removed, wipes over the bandage or cast with a wet hand.
